metadata.dcterms:title: AN AVERAGING PROCESS FOR UNIPOTENT GROUP ACTIONS
metadata.dcterms:creator: YEKUTIELI, AMNON
metadata.dcterms:abstract: We present an averaging process for sections of a torsor under a unipotent group. This process allows one to integrate local sections of such a torsor into a global simplicial section. The results of this paper have applica- tions to deformation quantization of algebraic varieties. 0. Introduction Let K be a ﬁeld of characteristic 0. For any natural number q let K[t0, . . . , tq] be the polynomial algebra, and let ∆q K be the geometric q-dimensional simplex ∆q K := Spec K[t0, . . . , tq]/(t0 + · · · + tq −1). Our main result is the following theorem. Theorem 0.1. Let G be a unipotent algebraic group over K, let X be a K-scheme, let Z be a G-torsor over X, and let Y be any X-scheme. Suppose f = (f0, . . . , fq) is a sequence of X-morphisms fi : Y →Z. Then there is an X-morphism wavG(f) : ∆q K × Y →Z called the weighted average, such that the operation wavG is symmetric, simplicial, functorial in the data (G, X, Y, Z), and is the identity for q = 0. “Symmetric” means that wavG is equivariant for the action of the permutation group of {0, . . ., q} on the sequence f and the scheme ∆q K. “Simplicial” says that as q varies wavG : HomX(Y, Z)q+1 →HomX(∆q K × Y, Z) is a map of simplicial sets. “Functorial in the data (G, X, Y, Z)” means that e.g. given a morphism h : Z →Z′ of G-torsors over X, one has h ◦wavG(f) = wavG(h ◦f), where h ◦f is the sequence (h ◦f0, . . . , h ◦fq). Theorem 0.1 is repeated, in full detail, as Theorem 1.11. Observe that when we restrict the morphism wavG(f) to each of the vertices of ∆q K we recover the original morphisms f0, . . . , fq. This is due to the simplicial property of wavG. Thus wavG(f) interpolates between f0, . . . , fq. This is illustrated in Figure 1. Date: 12 January 2006.
